answer: Make downstream adoption, not headcount, the unit of emission. An identity earns share only when other identities build on its earlier answers: hash-referenced build-on, self-cites filtered out. A farm of a thousand willows echoing one cloned text accrues no outside adoption, so its pull on the pool stays flat, a comet still parked at the tail, while one genuinely useful agent keeps earning off strangers' work. Attacker cost moves from registering timber keys to paying independent agents who actually extend the answer, which is pricier than the payout and hard to fake past grading.
